drafts.spl: index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog:Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational" EventCode=1 Image="*powershell*" (CommandLine="*-enc*" OR CommandLine="*-EncodedCommand*") ParentImage="*.exe" | where match(ParentImage, "(?i)\\\\(winword|excel|outlook)\.exe$") | where match(Image, "(?i)\\\\powershell(_ise)?\.exe$") | where match(CommandLine, "(?i)\s-(enc|encodedcommand)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}") | stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(CommandLine) as CommandLine by Computer, User, ParentImage, Image

findings.detail: The 4th where clause reduces to a near-tautology that actually EXCLUDES the primary attack. Operator precedence makes it `(NOT match(CommandLine,encPattern)) OR match(CommandLine,suspicious) OR (NOT match(ParentCommandLine,officeExt))`. Because the prior where already forced match(CommandLine,encPattern)=TRUE, the first term is always FALSE, leaving `match(CommandLine,suspicious) OR NOT match(ParentCommandLine,officeExt)`. Consequence: when a macro document is opened normally, ParentCommandLine contains the document path (e.g. .docm/.xlsm), so NOT match(ParentCommandLine,officeExt)=FALSE; if the powershell line carries only -enc <base64> (no -nop/iex/http/etc.) then match(suspicious)=FALSE and the whole row is DROPPED. The canonical maldoc->powershell -enc chain is silently suppressed.
findings.fix_hint: Remove this clause entirely; detecting Office->powershell with -enc base64 (steps 1-2) needs no extra keyword gate. If enrichment is wanted, compute suspicious flags in eval and keep them as context, not as a pass/fail filter.

findings.detail: Image filter `(?i)\\powershell(_ise)?\.exe$` only matches powershell.exe / powershell_ise.exe. A copied/renamed interpreter (powershel1.exe, pwsh.exe PowerShell 7/Core, or any random name) still accepts -EncodedCommand and fully evades. Matching on Image path leaf is brittle; OriginalFileName/Description are ignored.
findings.fix_hint: Match on OriginalFileName="PowerShell.EXE" OR Description, and include pwsh.exe, so renamed binaries are caught regardless of on-disk name.

findings.detail: The -enc regex `\s-(enc|encodedcommand|e|ec)\s+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` only matches the literal abbreviations enc/encodedcommand/e/ec and requires whitespace before the base64. PowerShell accepts any unambiguous prefix (-en, -enco, -encod, -encode, -encoded) and a colon separator (-enc:BASE64 / -EncodedCommand:BASE64). Variants like `-encod <b64>` or `-enc:<b64>` are not matched and evade.
findings.fix_hint: Broaden to `-e(n(c(o(d(e(d(c(o(m(m(a(n(d)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?)?` style or simpler `-e[a-z]*` and allow `[\s:]+` as the separator before the base64 blob.

findings.detail: ParentImage is restricted to winword|excel|outlook. Other Office/suite hosts that execute macros and spawn powershell are not covered: POWERPNT.EXE (PowerPoint), MSACCESS.EXE, MSPUB.EXE, VISIO.EXE, and LOLBin relays like mshta.exe/wscript.exe/cscript.exe. A PowerPoint macro spawning encoded powershell fully evades.
findings.fix_hint: Extend the ParentImage alternation to include powerpnt|msaccess|mspub|visio (and consider script hosts) per the office-spawns-interpreter intent.

findings.detail: Detection depends on exact Image/ParentImage path leaves and the base64 charset pattern; if ParentImage or CommandLine is absent/empty the match() returns false and the event is dropped. Also the encPattern regex is evaluated twice (where #3 and inside where #4), redundant CPU over every EventCode=1 event.
findings.fix_hint: Precompute match() results once with eval into boolean fields and reference them; guard for missing fields with coalesce/isnotnull.

findings.detail: Both surviving sample_rows (WINWORD->powershell for CORP\jdoe, OUTLOOK->powershell for CORP\bwayne) are plausible legitimate admin/add-in activity; volume is tiny (0.28/day) so no flood risk, but encoded-command use by sanctioned tooling (e.g. ConfigMgr, add-ins) could generate benign hits.
findings.fix_hint: Allowlist known-good signing/parent contexts or correlate with IntegrityLevel and subsequent network/child-process activity before alerting.

evasion_events.note: Renamed/alternate interpreter: Image is pwsh.exe (PowerShell 7) dropped to Temp. Image regex `\\powershell(_ise)?\.exe$` does not match pwsh.exe, so the attack chain is missed though -enc base64 is present.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS04.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -encod SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAKQA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\bwayne</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\EXCEL.EXE"</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Prefix-abbreviation evasion: `-encod` is a valid unambiguous prefix of -EncodedCommand but is not in the regex alternation (enc|encodedcommand|e|ec), and the trailing char 'd' breaks the `-enc\s+` requirement, so where #3 fails to match.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS02.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc:SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAKQA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Colon-separator evasion: PowerShell accepts `-enc:<base64>`. The regex requires `\s+` between the flag and the blob, so `-enc:` is not matched and the event is dropped.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS03.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAKQA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\POWERPNT.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Alternate Office parent: PowerPoint (POWERPNT.EXE) macro spawns powershell -enc base64. ParentImage alternation only lists winword|excel|outlook, so where #1 fails despite a valid Office-macro attack chain.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAKQA=</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n "C:\Users\jdoe\Downloads\invoice.docm"</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Exploits the broken 4th where clause: this is the canonical maldoc chain (WINWORD opening invoice.docm spawns powershell -enc base64 with no extra flags). Because ParentCommandLine contains .docm, NOT match(ParentCommandLine,officeExt)=FALSE and the plain -enc line has no suspicious keyword, so match(suspicious)=FALSE -> row is dropped. The most realistic attack is silently excluded.

findings.detail: Image detection still matches only the path leaf via `(?i)\\(powershell(_ise)?|pwsh)\.exe$`. pwsh/powershell_ise are now covered (prior finding partially resolved), but a copied/renamed interpreter still fully evades. Sysmon ships OriginalFileName and Description for EventID=1; a renamed powershell.exe (e.g. updater.exe, svchost.exe copy) keeps OriginalFileName=PowerShell.EXE but presents an arbitrary Image leaf, so the `img` where-clause returns false and the Office->encoded-PowerShell chain is dropped. Attack_step 1/2 (Office spawns powershell with -enc) is defeated with a trivial copy+rename.
findings.fix_hint: Add an OR on OriginalFileName/Description (match on OriginalFileName=powershell.exe/pwsh.exe or Description='Windows PowerShell') in addition to the Image leaf, so renamed copies are still caught.

findings.detail: Schedule is cron */15 with a 20m lookback window, giving a 5-minute overlap every run. A single Office->powershell -enc event within the overlap region can be alerted twice. Low impact given 0.14 hits/day but produces duplicate notables.
findings.fix_hint: Align window to the cron interval (15m) or dedupe on event identity (_time+Computer+Image+CommandLine) in the stats.

findings.detail: coalesce defaults pimg/img/cmd to empty string, but match() on empty returns false, so any EventID=1 with ParentImage, Image or CommandLine absent/empty is silently dropped. A truncated/parsing-failed Sysmon record carrying the real chain evades. Inherent to path-leaf matching but worth noting.
findings.fix_hint: Alert (or route to a review queue) on EventID=1 where Image matches powershell but ParentImage/CommandLine is null, rather than dropping silently.

findings.detail: sample_rows shows WINWORD.EXE -> powershell.exe for CORP\jdoe surviving the filter. Legitimate Office add-ins, ConfigMgr/SCCM tooling and signed management scripts occasionally launch powershell with -EncodedCommand from an Office host. Volume is tiny (0.14/day) so no flood, but sanctioned encoded-command use will generate occasional benign hits.
findings.fix_hint: Enrich with signature/signer status (Signed=true, trusted signer) or a known-good add-in allowlist on Image hash before alerting.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Temp\updater.exe</Data><Data Name='OriginalFileName'>PowerShell.EXE</Data><Data Name='Description'>Windows PowerShell</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Users\jdoe\AppData\Local\Temp\updater.exe" -enc SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZQBiAEMAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkA</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n "C:\Users\jdoe\invoice.docm"</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Renamed PowerShell copy: ParentImage=WINWORD.EXE (satisfies parent regex) and CommandLine carries `-enc <base64>` (satisfies cmd regex), but Image leaf is updater.exe so `match(img,(?i)\\(powershell(_ise)?|pwsh)\.exe$)` is false and the event is dropped. OriginalFileName=PowerShell.EXE / Description='Windows PowerShell' prove the binary identity, which the search ignores. An improved search keying on OriginalFileName/Description must match this.

findings.detail: The CommandLine regex `(?i)\s-e[a-z]*[\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` requires the first char after the `-enc` separator to be in the base64 class. PowerShell happily accepts the encoded blob quoted: `-enc "<base64>"` or `-enc '<base64>'`. The `[\s:]+` cannot consume the quote and `"`/`'` are not in `[A-Za-z0-9+/=]`, so the match fails. Office->powershell with a quote-wrapped encoded command (attack_step 1/2) is fully and trivially evaded while ParentImage stays WINWORD.EXE.
findings.fix_hint: Allow an optional quote between the separator and the blob, e.g. `[\s:]+["']?[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}`, and/or match on OriginalFileName/Description plus a `-e`-token test independent of the payload delimiter.

findings.detail: Detection assumes Office is the DIRECT parent of the encoded-PowerShell process. Maldoc chains almost always interpose a launcher: Office -> cmd.exe /c powershell -enc, Office -> wscript/cscript -> powershell, Office -> mshta -> powershell, or Office spawns via WMI (ParentImage=WmiPrvSE.exe) or explorer. In every case the powershell EventID=1 record carries ParentImage=cmd.exe/wscript.exe/etc., the `pimg` Office regex returns false, and the whole chain is dropped. This is the single most common real-world variant and is fully missed.
findings.fix_hint: Do not require Office as the immediate parent: detect `powershell -enc` broadly and correlate ancestry (join on ProcessGuid/ParentProcessGuid or a lookback join) so Office is anywhere in the lineage; or also include cmd/wscript/cscript/mshta/wmiprvse as parents.

findings.detail: The regex only keys on the literal `-e...` flag. An attacker achieves the same base64-payload execution without `-EncodedCommand`: `powershell -nop -c "IEX([Convert]::FromBase64String('...'))"`, `-ep bypass -c`, gzip/IO.Compression stagers, or reading the blob from an env var/clipboard/file. There is no `-e<base64>` token, so the search never fires even though ParentImage is Office. This defeats the detection intent even if it sits just outside the narrowly-worded attack_step.
findings.fix_hint: Add a secondary branch for base64 decoding primitives (FromBase64String, GzipStream, [Convert], -EncodedArguments) and for `-c`/`-Command` long encoded literals, not just the `-e` flag.

findings.detail: The `{20,}` floor assumes a long blob. 20 base64 chars ~= 15 bytes ~= 7 UTF-16LE chars, so a short encoded stager (e.g. `-enc` of `iex $env:a` or a one-liner referencing a preset variable) encodes to under 20 chars and slips below the threshold while remaining a valid Office->encoded-PowerShell execution.
findings.fix_hint: Lower the floor to ~8-10 (a valid UTF-16LE EncodedCommand is a multiple of 4 and at least a few chars) or drop the length gate and rely on the `-enc` token + optional base64 shape.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>"C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" -nop -w hidden -enc "SQBFAFgAIAAoAE4AZQB3AC0ATwBiAGoAZQBjAHQAIABOAGUAdAAuAFcAZQBiAEMAbABpAGUAbgB0ACkA"</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Quote-wrapped encoded command. ParentImage is Office and -enc + a 60+ char base64 blob are present, but the leading double-quote after the separator falls outside `[A-Za-z0-9+/=]`, so `[\s:]+[A-Za-z0-9+/=]{20,}` never matches. Search misses it; it should fire.

Classic maldoc interposed launcher: WINWORD spawned cmd.exe which spawned powershell -enc. The powershell record carries ParentImage=cmd.exe, so the Office `pimg` regex returns false and the chain is dropped even though CommandLine clearly contains -enc+base64.

evasion_events.raw: <Event xmlns='http://schemas.microsoft.com/win/2004/08/events/event'><System><Provider Name='Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon' Guid='{5770385f-c22a-43e0-bf4c-06f5698ffbd9}'/><EventID>1</EventID><Computer>WS01.corp.local</Computer></System><EventData><Data Name='Image'>C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe</Data><Data Name='CommandLine'>powershell.exe -nop -w hidden -c "IEX([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String('SQBFAFgAKABOAGUAdwAtAE8AYgBqAGUAYwB0ACkA')))"</Data><Data Name='User'>CORP\jdoe</Data><Data Name='ParentImage'>C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE</Data><Data Name='ParentCommandLine'>"C:\Program Files\Microsoft Office\root\Office16\WINWORD.EXE" /n</Data></EventData></Event>
evasion_events.note: Same base64 execution without the -enc flag: Office->powershell using -c and FromBase64String. ParentImage is Office but there is no `-e<base64>` token, so the CommandLine where-clause never matches.
